prusa_steps: **Fastest:** File › Open Project (Ctrl+O) › `cad/print/plates/plate_X.3mf`. The parts are already on the bed AND every setting on the plate's page is inside (printer CR-6 SE, PETG, layers, infill, supports): answer **Yes** to load its settings, then slice. Part already printed? Right-click it in the object list › Delete.
Top right: switch the mode to **Expert** (red). Otherwise half of these fields are hidden.
Printer (once): Configuration › Configuration Wizard › Creality › **CR-6 SE**. Filament: Generic PETG.
Lost? **Ctrl+F** searches every setting by name (type "support", "brim", "infill"…) and jumps to it.

Make 3 print presets once: set DRAFT (plates B, C), STANDARD (A, D), DETAIL (E), click the **save icon** next to the preset name and call them "PETG Draft / Standard / Detail". Then each plate = pick the preset in the right panel + the plate's few changes.
Changed fields turn **orange** with an unlocked padlock; click the orange arrow to undo a change.
prusa_keys: import STL (or drag the files in)
arrange the parts on the bed
place on face: click the flat face that goes down
Plater / Print / Filament / Printer settings tabs
switch 3D view ↔ Preview (layers, supports, estimated time bottom right)
export G-code: short name, no spaces (e.g. PLATEB.gcode), to the SD card
prusa_map: Print Settings › **Layers and perimeters** › Layer height
Print Settings › Layers and perimeters › Vertical shells › **Perimeters**
Print Settings › Layers and perimeters › Horizontal shells › **Solid layers** Top / Bottom
Print Settings › Layers and perimeters › Advanced › Seam position: **Rear** / Aligned
Print Settings › **Infill** › Fill density, Fill pattern (Grid, Gyroid, Rectilinear = lines)
Print Settings › **Skirt and brim** › Loops (minimum) = 2; Brim type Outer only, Brim width 5 mm (plate A)
Print Settings › **Support material** › Generate support material ✓, Auto generated supports ✓
Support material › **On build plate only** ✓, Overhang threshold 50°
Support material › Top contact Z distance 0.25, XY separation 0.8 mm, Top interface layers 2
Support material › Options for support material › Pattern **Rectilinear**, Pattern spacing **2.5 mm** (≈15 %)
Print Settings › **Speed** › Perimeters, Small perimeters, External perimeters, Infill, Solid / Top solid infill, Travel, First layer speed
Print Settings › **Advanced** › Extrusion width 0.42; Elephant foot compensation 0.15 mm
Filament Settings › **Filament** › Temperature: First layer 238 / 80, Other layers 235 / 80
Filament Settings › **Cooling** › Min / max fan speed 30 %, Disable fan for the first 3 layers
Filament Settings › **Advanced** › Max volumetric speed 8 mm³/s
Printer Settings › **Extruder 1** › Retraction length 5 mm, speed 40 mm/s
common: Textured PEI sheet, 80 °C. **No glue.** Clean it with dish soap + water (or isopropyl) and don't touch the print area
a little higher than for PLA: PETG must not be squished into PEI (it can stick too hard)
let the bed cool to room temperature, take the sheet off and flex it: parts pop off
keep under 8 mm³/s (stock CR-6 SE hotend): the speeds below already do

parts.fix: Check each hole as in the build guide, section 2: it tells you how much to sand the real parts
Peel the brim. Pivot screw binds: open the hole with a 5/32 in (4 mm) drill turned by hand

support_rows: **touching build plate only** (no supports on the part)

parts.accurate: 6807 bearing pocket (47.1 mm), MG996R screw holes
parts.fix: Bearing tight: sand the pocket wall (120 grit on a finger) until it presses in with thumbs. Loose: one layer of tape. Clear support bits out of the servo pocket with pliers

parts.accurate: lift-servo screw holes, screw holes at the ends
parts.fix: Run each screw in once and back out before final assembly
Rod won't go in: drill 6 mm, 8 mm deep (tape flag on the bit)

parts.accurate: nothing critical: board pegs, 2 screw tabs
parts.fix: Peg too fat for a board hole: shave it with a knife. Snapped peg: a dab of hot glue holds the board

support_rows: **touching build plate only** (no supports on the part)

parts.accurate: hub into the bearing (34.95 mm), 2 rod holes (6.0 mm), horn screw holes
parts.fix: Hub tight: sand it evenly, turning it. Rod holes tight: drill 6 mm (or 15/64 in) by hand

parts.accurate: 4 LM6UU pockets (12.15 mm) in line, wrist-servo screws, link pivot
parts.fix: Pockets print on their side, so the top of each droops: ream with a 12 mm drill or sandpaper on a 12 mm dowel / marker until the LM6UU presses in; the carriage must slide down both rods by its own weight

support_rows: **touching build plate only** (no supports on the part)

parts.fix: Remove supports, file only the pad area, never the teeth. Bore tight: twist a 5/32 in drill through by hand
Spline socket tight: scrape lightly inside with the knife tip, test the SG90 spline after every pass. Never file the teeth

parts.accurate: gear axle hole and servo position: they set the gear mesh
parts.fix: Don't open the axle hole more than needed: the gears must mesh without play
